title: A fixed 35.23-day HARPS wave increases GJ 433 HIRES error in 31 nights
abstract: We test whether a selected 35.23-day GJ 433 HARPS residual predicts independent HIRES velocities. We fit its amplitude and phase in 85 HARPS nights and transfer the fixed wave to 31 HIRES nights. With a quadratic trend, two known-period waves and a HIRES upgrade offset, the extra wave increases weighted squared error by 34.3 percent. All 36 reduction, trend, error and offset controls also increase error. All 25 period controls from 35.21 to 35.33 days increase error. Four grouped contribution bootstrap ranges include zero. The result gives no independent confirmation of the selected wave. It does not exclude a smaller signal, refute the known system or identify the cause of the HARPS peak. Sparse nights, fixed training coefficients, a simple long-orbit trend and unknown stellar noise limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.
